heading: Oklahoma Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Oklahoma paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Oklahoma income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Oklahoma introduced lower income tax rates in 2026, potentially increasing take-home pay for employees whose other payroll circumstances remain unchanged.

Whether you work in Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Norman, Edmond or another Oklahoma community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare employment opportunities, manage expenses and plan your savings.

## How to Use the Oklahoma Paycheck Calculator

Start by selecting whether you receive annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross compensation before taxes and deductions. Hourly employees should provide their hourly rate, regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Oklahoma income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions and health insurance premiums. Enter the full tax amounts, including any extra withholding.

Review the estimated paycheck breakdown to understand your individual deductions and remaining net earnings.

For greater accuracy, compare your calculator inputs with your latest pay stub.

## Oklahoma Payroll Taxes in 2026

The [Oklahoma Tax Commission](https://oklahoma.gov/tax.html) publishes official information about state income taxes, employer withholding and annual tax changes.

## How Oklahoma State Income Tax Works

Oklahoma uses a progressive income tax system. Different portions of applicable taxable income are subject to different rates.

For 2026, the state simplified its income tax structure and reduced its highest marginal rate to 4.5%.

The annual tax brackets for single and married filing separately taxpayers are:

Joint filers and certain other filing categories use different thresholds.

These are annual income tax return brackets rather than the wage thresholds employers use for paycheck withholding.

Employers follow the applicable payroll percentage tables, which incorporate withholding allowances and relevant payroll-period adjustments.

Review the [Oklahoma Tax Commission publications directory](https://oklahoma.gov/tax/reporting-resources/publications.html) for official tax-year documents.

## Understanding Oklahoma Form OK-W-4

Oklahoma employees generally complete Form OK-W-4 to provide their state withholding information.

The certificate communicates the employee's withholding classification, allowances and applicable additional withholding.

Each ordinary withholding allowance has an annual value of $1,000.

The amount is distributed across the applicable number of payroll periods.

These allowances reduce the wages used to calculate state withholding. They are not direct cash payments or tax credits.

Your Oklahoma withholding certificate is separate from federal Form W-4. Updating one does not necessarily update the other.

Consult the [official Oklahoma 2026 employer withholding booklet](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/publications/businesses/withholding-tables/WHTables-2026.pdf) for instructions.

## How to Calculate Oklahoma Income Tax Withholding

The Oklahoma employer percentage method subtracts applicable withholding allowances from taxable wages before applying the relevant payroll-period table.

For employees using the single withholding classification and receiving biweekly wages, the 2026 percentage table is:

parts.caption: How to Calculate Oklahoma Income Tax Withholding

parts.markdown:
Suppose you receive $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages and claim one ordinary withholding allowance.

Adjusted taxable wages:

$2,500 − $38.46 = $2,461.54

Oklahoma withholding:

$4.20 + (($2,461.54 − $521) × 4.5%)

Estimated state withholding: $91.52.

This example assumes ordinary taxable employment and no additional withholding requests.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Oklahoma Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal withholding depends on taxable wages, filing status, pay frequency and information entered on Form W-4.

Employers use the procedures described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Employees with multiple jobs, additional income or qualifying credits may have different withholding amounts.

The [IRS Tax Withholding Estimator](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-withholding-estimator) can help evaluate whether your federal withholding is appropriate.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

The annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500 in 2026.

You can review historical contribution limits through the [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html).

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Consult [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for official federal payroll contribution requirements.

Assume the employee uses ordinary single federal withholding settings, claims one Oklahoma withholding allowance and has no additional benefit deductions.

Actual paycheck amounts may differ because of withholding elections, benefits and employer rounding methods.

## Oklahoma Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can calculate gross earnings by multiplying their hourly wage by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 6 = $225

Total gross earnings: $1,225.

Federal and Oklahoma taxes are then calculated using the applicable taxable wage amounts.

Review the [Oklahoma Department of Labor](https://oklahoma.gov/labor.html) and [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about employee eligibility.

## Does Oklahoma Have Local Income Taxes?

Oklahoma municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employees.

However, local sales taxes, housing costs, insurance premiums and transportation expenses may influence household purchasing power.

When comparing employment offers in Tulsa and Oklahoma City, calculate your estimated net salary first and then compare expected living expenses separately.

## Working in Oklahoma and Living in Texas

Employees living near the Oklahoma–Texas border may work in one state while residing in another.

Although Texas does not impose individual state income tax on ordinary wages, qualifying Oklahoma-sourced employment income may still be subject to Oklahoma income tax.

Your residence, employment location and income sourcing determine the applicable tax treatment.

Consult the Oklahoma Tax Commission before claiming a nonresident withholding exemption.

## Managing Your Oklahoma Take-Home Pay

Create your monthly budget using estimated net earnings rather than your gross annual salary.

Account for housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, insurance and required debt payments.

The [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/) provides educational resources for managing everyday financial decisions.

Use our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to establish a savings target, and our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) to compare compensation arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Oklahoma's income tax rate in 2026?

Oklahoma uses progressive income tax rates with a maximum ordinary rate of 4.5%. Actual paycheck withholding depends on applicable wage thresholds and allowances.

### How much is one Oklahoma withholding allowance worth?

Each ordinary withholding allowance has an annual value of $1,000, distributed across the applicable payroll periods.

### Does Oklahoma City have a separate employee income tax?

Oklahoma City generally does not impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax. Federal and Oklahoma income taxes still apply where appropriate.
